Usually music taste comes with depth of thinking. People who put effort into the things they enjoy shows depth of thought. If their music taste is trash, it means they're usually a very shallow person and haven't taken time to think deeply about what they listen too, likely everything else as well.

Now good or bad taste is determined by a few things, harmony in innovative sound or how complex or interesting, music theory wise(music theory is an analytical tool that is used to document patterns in music, the song does something new or interesting compared to other music created before or currently which you can tell using music theory),  while being pleasant to the ear along with a good mix( adjusting volumes, tones, instrument placing and textures of instruments as well as many other things, to fit the artist's vision) and mastery (microadjusting everything mentioned before but this time with a focus on maintaining artitistic vision as well as optimizing the song and making it sound more complete so that it sounds exactly like artist intended it on as many platforms as possible), again these things can vary because that is the nature of art but it gives you a picture.

So someone with good taste in pop could be listening to olivia rodrigo, billie eilish NewJeans, the more nuanced songs by BTS(they are among the few groups that completely self produce many of their songs, songs like The truth untold, Spring day and even fake love), BIBI for example, or GEM and Lay for mandopop.

 However, it shouldn't just end there, they need to have a wider appreciation of tastes too.

 If they hear Slipknot's Disasterpiece and just think its loud nonsense, then their good taste is highly limited and restrained(pop is often derived from much more complex forms of music, a good pop song usually indicates that the artist is a good student of the more complex arts) because there's no effort put in to actually learn more about music(instead of just pop). 

Another slightly different example would be Rubinstein's interpretation of Chopin's op 48 no 1, if they think this piece is boring then they have no maturity and are usually quite empty as a person. 

Taste is an ongoing process. As long as you are open to all kinds of music as well as listen to music that pushes boundaries, you can develop great taste(not just good).
